guide.title: Ardeatino, Rome: the Appian catacombs, the Fosse Ardeatine and the Tre Fontane abbey
guide.intro: Ardeatino is the twentieth of Rome's quartieri, Q. XX in the official series. It lies outside the Aurelian Walls, along the II, III and IV miles of the via Appia Antica and along the via Ardeatina, and much of it is not street at all but pozzolana country: quarries, catacomb galleries, tomb-lined stretches of Roman road and a two-hundred-hectare estate of farmland inside the city. The Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra lists seven catacombs open to the public in Rome, and three of them are here, each with published hours and a guided visit. Above one of them stands a basilica of the seven-church pilgrimage holding the stone with the footprints of the Quo Vadis story. On the via Ardeatina, the quarries where 335 people were shot in March 1944 are now a memorial with a museum. South-west, on via di Acque Salvie, a Trappist abbey keeps three churches, a shop and a porter's lodge.

sections.heading: The boundaries of Ardeatino
sections.body:
A quartiere is a much larger thing than a rione, and this one is drawn by roads. it.wikipedia's article on Ardeatino gives the perimeter: via Appia Antica divides it from Q. IX Appio-Latino in the stretch from the Aurelian Walls at Porta San Sebastiano to via Cecilia Metella; via Laurentina divides it from Q. XXXII Europa between viale dell'Atletica and via Cristoforo Colombo; via Cristoforo Colombo continues the line to via di Porta Ardeatina; and the rioni San Saba and Celio lie to the north. Past via Cecilia Metella the line moves off the road, and both sides of the Appia at the IV mile fall inside the quartiere.

That has consequences a visitor will notice on the ground, because several famous things on this road are not in this quartiere. The church of the Domine Quo Vadis, at the fork where the Ardeatina leaves the Appia, is in Appio-Latino, and so are the Colonna di Pio IX standing on the far side of the Appia from San Sebastiano, the Mausoleo di Cecilia Metella, the Castrum Caetani and the deconsecrated church of San Nicola a Capo di Bove that stands inside the castle courtyard. The stone with the footprints of the Quo Vadis story is in the Cappella delle Reliquie of San Sebastiano fuori le mura, which is in Ardeatino, and the slab in the Appio-Latino church is a copy of it.

The Aurelian Walls and Porta Ardeatina are the northern boundary itself, and a boundary belongs to neither of the units it divides. Via Appia Antica is the boundary for part of its course here, and it runs far beyond the quartiere in both directions; the sources give position along it as an address and by the mile. Tre Fontane is inside the quartiere: the declared line to the west is via Laurentina, and the abbey stands east of it on via di Acque Salvie.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Steer by bus lines and street numbers, which the operators publish.

The Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra gives ATAC 118 and 218 for the Catacombe di San Callisto at Via Appia Antica 110, and ATAC 30, 130, 160, 670, 174 and 716 for the Catacombe di Domitilla at Via delle Sette Chiese 282. The operator of the Catacombe di San Sebastiano, at Via Appia Antica 136, gives three routes to the stop called Catacombe di San Sebastiano: bus 660 from Metro A Arco di Travertino, bus 118 from Metro B Colosseo or Circo Massimo, and bus 218 from Metro A San Giovanni, alighting at Fosse Ardeatine and continuing 300 metres along Vicolo delle Sette Chiese. The Parco archeologico dell'Appia antica gives Metro A Arco di Travertino with bus 660, Metro A Colli Albani with bus 663, or bus 118 from the historic centre for Capo di Bove at Via Appia Antica 222.

The other addresses to put into a map: Via Ardeatina 174 for the Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine; Via di Acque Salvie 1 for the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane, off via Laurentina; Via Appia Antica 42 for the Ex Cartiera Latina and the regional park authority; Viale di Tor Marancia 63 for the Museo Condominiale di Tor Marancia; Piazza Lante and Via Francesco Belloni, both off Via Giulio Aristide Sartorio, and Viale Londra for the three entrances to the Tenuta di Tor Marancia. The regional park authority also runs bicycle hire; no address is stated for it, so none is given here.

sections.heading: Hours, tickets and access
sections.body:
The three ticketed catacombs are guided sites and their published terms differ. San Callisto opens 09:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 17:00, with tours starting every 30 minutes and lasting about 40, a minimum of two people per tour and the ticket desk shutting at 16:50; the last afternoon tour starts at 16:30 on Maundy Thursday. The catacombs are closed every Wednesday, on 1 January and on 25 December, and for an annual winter closure. The dates published for that closure have not been updated, so none are given here. Tickets are 10 euro full and 7 euro reduced.

San Sebastiano opens Tuesday to Sunday 09:15 to 17:15, last entry 16:45. It is closed on Mondays, on 25 December, 1 January and Easter Day, and from 7 to 27 December 2026. Tickets are 10 euro full and 7 euro reduced, visits are led by an in-house guide, and the operator lists Italian, English, French, Spanish and German. Domitilla opens Monday and Wednesday to Sunday, 09:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 17:00, with Tuesday as its weekly rest day; its published dates for an annual closure have not been updated, so none are given here.

Three further catacombs in the quartiere are not on the public visiting list. The Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra opens them on written request to protocollo@arcsacra.va, for groups of no more than fifteen, at 250 euro, accompanied by a fossore for custody and an archaeologist.

Above ground: the Basilica di San Sebastiano fuori le mura opens 08:15 to 18:00 from October to March and 08:15 to 19:00 from April to September. The Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine opens 08:15 to 15:15 Monday to Friday and 08:15 to 16:45 at weekends, with guided visits booked through ANFIM at info@anfim.org or +39 06 6795629. The Abbazia delle Tre Fontane complex opens every day 06:30 to 20:45; Santa Maria Scala Coeli 09:00 to 12:00 and 15:00 to 17:30; San Paolo alle Tre Fontane 07:30 to 20:00; the monastic shop Monday to Saturday 08:30 to 19:30 and Sunday 09:00 to 13:30. The green area and car park at the Ex Cartiera Latina open 08:30 to 17:00 in winter and 08:30 to 19:00 in summer, and the Tenuta di Tor Marancia is described by the state park as freely accessible. One site is shut: the Complesso di Capo di Bove has been closed to the public since 22 June 2026 for restoration works, and no reopening date has been announced.

faq.question: Are the catacombs Vatican territory?
faq.answer: No. They stand on Italian soil in this quartiere, and a visitor there is under Italian law. The Holy See's own published list of its extraterritorial properties in Rome names thirteen holdings and contains no catacomb, no basilica on the Appia and nothing on the via Ardeatina. What is true is a different arrangement: under article 33 of the 1929 Concordat, confirmed by article 12 of the 1984 Accordo, the Holy See retains the disponibilita of the Christian catacombs together with the burden of their custody, maintenance and conservation. The Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra governs them, the callistian complex is the property of APSA, and the Salesians of Don Bosco have run the welcome and the guided visits at San Callisto since 1930.

faq.question: Which catacombs can you actually visit, and how?
faq.answer: Three sell tickets and run guided tours: San Callisto at Via Appia Antica 110, San Sebastiano at Via Appia Antica 136 and Domitilla at Via delle Sette Chiese 282. All three are visited with a guide rather than alone, and San Callisto requires a minimum of two people per tour. Three others in the quartiere are on the Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra's list of catacombs opened on request: the Museo di Domitilla with the Regione dei Fornai, the Museo della Torretta with the Cripte di Lucina, and the Catacomba di Vigna Chiaraviglio. Those are booked by written request to protocollo@arcsacra.va, for groups of no more than fifteen, at 250 euro, accompanied by a fossore for custody and an archaeologist. Two more, the catacombs of Balbina and of Santi Marco e Marcelliano, have no stated visiting arrangements at all.

faq.question: Where is the Quo Vadis stone?
faq.answer: In the Cappella delle Reliquie of the Basilica di San Sebastiano fuori le mura, at Via Appia Antica 136, which is in this quartiere. The chapel was commissioned by Maximilian, Duke of Bavaria, in 1625, and also holds an arrow of the martyrdom and the column Sebastian was bound to. The small church of the Domine Quo Vadis, at the fork where the via Ardeatina leaves the Appia, is in Appio-Latino; the slab shown there is a copy of the stone in San Sebastiano.

faq.question: Can you go inside the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane?
faq.answer: Yes. The abbey's own site gives the complex as open every day from 06:30 to 20:45, and it publishes hours for each church: Santi Vincenzo e Anastasio, the abbey church, on the same 06:30 to 20:45; Santa Maria Scala Coeli 09:00 to 12:00 and 15:00 to 17:30; and San Paolo alle Tre Fontane, which the abbey calls San Paolo al Martirio, 07:30 to 20:00. The monastic shop opens Monday to Saturday 08:30 to 19:30 and Sunday 09:00 to 13:30, and the porter's lodge keeps its own hours. The community is Trappist, that is Cistercians of the Strict Observance. The abbey brews beer, but no source states any brewery visit or taproom, so none is described here.

faq.question: What is at the Fosse Ardeatine?
faq.answer: The pozzolana quarries on via Ardeatina where German occupation forces shot 335 people on 24 March 1944, in reprisal for the partisan attack in via Rasella, and the memorial built over them. The sacrario holds 335 granite sacelli, in seven double rows in the order the bodies were exhumed, plus one more dedicated to the Martiri d'Italia; 328 of the dead are identified and seven are unknown, and 70 of the 335 were Jews. A museum of relics and documents sits inside the complex, behind the monumental slab. The site opens 08:15 to 15:15 Monday to Friday and 08:15 to 16:45 at weekends, and ANFIM runs the guided visits.

faq.question: Is there anything here that is free?
faq.answer: Several things. The Parco archeologico dell'Appia antica states that the Tenuta di Tor Marancia, two hundred hectares of Roman countryside with three entrances, is freely accessible. The Museo Condominiale di Tor Marancia is twenty-two murals painted on eleven blocks of a housing estate and is looked at from the street. The green area and car park at the Ex Cartiera Latina, the regional park's headquarters at Via Appia Antica 42, open daily without a ticket, and the park outside Forte Ardeatino has been open to the public since May 2006. The eight churches of the modern quartiere, from the Chiesa dell'Annunziatella, whose internal inscription is dated 12 August 1220, to San Josemaria Escriva of 1996, are places of worship rather than ticketed sites.

places.name: Catacombe di San Callisto
places.summary: Part of the callistian complex, an area of about thirty hectares between via Appia Antica, via Ardeatina and via delle Sette Chiese, with fifteen hectares of cemetery and galleries running to nearly twenty kilometres. Sixteen popes and more than fifty martyrs were buried here. The Cripta dei Papi carries the original Greek inscriptions of Pontian, Anterus, Fabian, Lucius I and Eutychian, the tomb of Sixtus II, and the metric inscription of Pope Damasus cut in the lettering devised by the calligrapher Furius Dionysius Filocalus. The adjoining crypt of St Cecilia keeps frescoes of the early ninth century; her relics were removed by Paschal I in 821. The Cubicoli dei Sacramenti open off a gallery of the late second century, and two apsed funerary buildings survive above ground. Open 09:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 17:00, with tours every 30 minutes lasting about 40 minutes, a minimum of two people, and the ticket desk closing at 16:50. The catacombs are closed every Wednesday, on 1 January and on 25 December, and for an annual winter closure. The dates published for that closure have not been updated, so none are given here. Tickets 10 euro full, 7 euro reduced. ATAC 118 and 218.
places.history: The cemetery is named for the deacon Callistus, put in charge of it by Pope Zephyrinus, who reigned from 199 to 217, and himself pope from 217 to 222. Giovan Battista De Rossi excavated the complex between 1849 and 1854. The complex is the property of APSA, the Amministrazione del Patrimonio della Sede Apostolica; the Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra governs, guards and conserves it; and since 1930 the welcome of pilgrims and the guided visits have been entrusted to the Salesians of Don Bosco. It stands on Italian soil, and the Holy See retains the disponibilita of the Christian catacombs with the burden of their custody under article 33 of the 1929 Concordat, confirmed by article 12 of the 1984 Accordo.

places.name: Catacombe di San Sebastiano
places.summary: A hypogeum cemetery on the via Appia Antica, under the basilica of the same name. There are three levels of galleries; of four original levels the first is almost entirely destroyed. The piazzola, a former open-cast quarry, holds three mausolea cut into its walls, one of them the mausoleo degli Innocentiores. Above the infilled piazzola stands the triclia, a roofed colonnaded hall for funerary banquets whose walls carry more than 600 graffiti invoking Peter and Paul, together with a marble-lined edicola. Three martyrs are documented here: Sebastian, the Pannonian bishop Quirinus, and Eutychius. Open Tuesday to Sunday 09:15 to 17:15, last entry 16:45. Closed on Mondays, on 25 December, 1 January and Easter Day, and from 7 to 27 December 2026. Tickets 10 euro full, 7 euro reduced. Visits are led by an in-house guide, in Italian, English, French, Spanish and German, and booking is advised.
places.history: The place was known in antiquity as in catacumbas, from the Greek kata kymbe, 'by the hollows' — a dip in the ground beside the Appia is still visible, and the area was worked for pozzolana before it was a cemetery. The word 'catacomb' descends from this toponym. From the third century the site was called in memoria apostolorum: the Depositio martyrum of the mid-fourth century records Peter in catacumbas on 29 June, and the Martirologio Geronimiano adds utrumque in catacumbas, Tusco et Basso consulibus, that is in 258.

places.name: Catacombe di Domitilla
places.address: Via delle Sette Chiese 282, 00147 Roma RM
places.summary: A catacomb on the ancient via Ardeatina, dug in the praedium Domitillae, the estate of Flavia Domitilla, a relative of Flavius Clemens, consul in 95. Its titular martyrs are Nereus and Achilleus, probably victims of the persecution of 304, buried in a large apsed basilica of the time of Pope Siricius, who reigned from 384 to 399, preceded by a narthex and divided into three aisles by columns on reused capitals. The complex also holds the ipogeo dei Flavi, begun as a private pagan hypogeum at the end of the second century and taking Christian burials through the third; the cubicolo di Veneranda; the arcosolium of the Apostoli Piccoli; and the cubicolo of the fossor Diogenes. Christian and pagan burials coexist here. Open Monday and Wednesday to Sunday, 09:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 17:00, with Tuesday as the weekly rest day; its published dates for an annual closure have not been updated, so none are given here. ATAC 30, 130, 160, 670, 174 and 716.
places.history: The catacomb stands on Italian soil in this quartiere; the Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra governs it, sets its hours and gives www.catacombedomitilla.it as its site. Via delle Sette Chiese, on which the entrance stands, runs from San Paolo across two quartieri.

places.name: Museo di Domitilla e Regione dei Fornai
places.address: Via delle Sette Chiese 282, 00147 Roma RM
places.summary: A museum and a burial region inside the Domitilla complex, at the same address as the catacomb but under a different arrangement. This catacomb is not on the public visiting list. The Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra opens it on written request to protocollo@arcsacra.va, for groups of no more than fifteen, at 250 euro, accompanied by a fossore for custody and an archaeologist.
places.history: No source states a separate institutional history for the museum.

places.name: Museo della Torretta e Cripte di Lucina
places.summary: A museum and a group of crypts inside the callistian complex, sharing the San Callisto address. This catacomb is not on the public visiting list. The Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra opens it on written request to protocollo@arcsacra.va, for groups of no more than fifteen, at 250 euro, accompanied by a fossore for custody and an archaeologist.
places.history: No source states a separate institutional history for the museum.

places.name: Catacomba di Vigna Chiaraviglio
places.summary: A catacomb on the via Appia Antica between the San Callisto and San Sebastiano complexes. This catacomb is not on the public visiting list. The Pontificia Commissione di Archeologia Sacra opens it on written request to protocollo@arcsacra.va, for groups of no more than fifteen, at 250 euro, accompanied by a fossore for custody and an archaeologist.
places.history: No source states a history of the site beyond its place on the Commissione's list of catacombs opened on request.

places.name: Catacomba dei Santi Marco e Marcelliano
places.summary: A funerary area of the callistian complex, between via Appia Antica and via Ardeatina. It was anciently the cimitero di Basileo ad sanctum Marcum et Marcellianum, named first for the landowner and then for the martyrs. A second above-ground basilica held the tomb Pope Damasus chose for himself, his mother Lorenza and his sister Irene; nothing of the above-ground structures survives. No visiting arrangements are stated for it, so none are given here.
places.history: Antonio Bosio explored the cemetery in 1596 and his account was published posthumously in Roma sotterranea in 1632. Giovan Battista de Rossi re-explored it in 1868. Joseph Wilpert identified it in systematic digs of 1902 to 1905 beneath the courtyard of the Istituto San Tarcisio on via Appia Antica, finding apsed structures and the cripta delle quattro colonne. Antonio Ferrua dug further in 1947, and Mons. Patrick Saint-Roch studied the topography.

places.name: Catacomba di Balbina
places.summary: The third funerary area of the callistian complex, between via Appia Antica and via Ardeatina. It is named in three early sources: the Depositio episcoporum, which records the burial of Pope Mark above ground in Balbinae between January and October 336; the Index coemeteriorum vetus, which calls it cymiterium Balbinae ad sanctum Marcum; and an inscription of one Sabinus reading in cymiteriu Balbinae in cripta noba. The identification of the site with the Balbina of those texts remains uncertain, and that uncertainty is part of the record. No visiting arrangements are stated for it, so none are given here.
places.history: On 3 September 1991 the Salesian Tarcisio Gazzola noticed, in a field of lucerne, marks tracing the plan of a circiform basilica 66 metres long and 27 metres wide, which has been identified with the Marcian basilica named in the sources. The remains lie on via Ardeatina and are treated here as part of this record rather than as a separate site.

places.name: Basilica di San Sebastiano fuori le mura
places.summary: A basilica on the via Appia Antica, above the catacomb of the same name, and a station of the seven-church pilgrimage. Inside, on the left wall at the entrance, is the near-intact carmen dedicated by Pope Damasus to the martyr Eutychius, cut in Filocalian lettering. The altar holds the urn with Sebastian's remains and Giuseppe Giorgetti's recumbent statue pierced by arrows. The Cappella Albani was raised by Clement XI for his family in 1706, faced in polychrome marbles and decorated for the martyr-pope Fabian, who reigned from 236 to 250. The Cappella delle Reliquie, commissioned by Maximilian, Duke of Bavaria, in 1625, holds an arrow of the martyrdom, the column Sebastian was bound to, and at its centre the stone of the 'Quo Vadis?' episode with the footprints impressed in it. The basilica is a Franciscan parish. Open 08:15 to 18:00 from October to March and 08:15 to 19:00 from April to September; parish office Tuesday and Thursday 15:30 to 17:30, Wednesday and Saturday 10:00 to 12:00, reduced in July and closed in August and on feast days.
places.history: A church was built here in the fourth century with the title of Saints Peter and Paul, on the spot to which their relics were moved in 258: a Constantinian circiform basilica of three aisles with a large quadrangular atrium, on the same model as Sant'Agnese on the Nomentana and San Lorenzo on the Tiburtina. Sebastian's relics were taken to St Peter's in 826 for fear of a Saracen raid, which came and destroyed the church; Pope Nicholas I, who reigned from 858 to 867, rebuilt it, and Honorius III reconsecrated the martyr's altar at the Cistercians' request. Cardinal Scipione Borghese ordered the seventeenth-century rebuilding in 1608, to a design by Flaminio Ponzio continued by Giovanni Vasanzio with Guido Reni as artistic director; the facade is dated 1612, and Annibale Durante carved the wooden ceiling in the same year to a design traditionally given to Vasanzio. The aisles were rebuilt in 1933 on the ambulatory of the fourth-century church. The parish was erected on 18 April 1714 by bull of Clement XI, and John XXIII created the cardinalatial title San Sebastiano alle Catacombe in 1960. A marble bust of the blessing Christ in the convent adjoining the basilica was identified in 2001, in research for the Clement XI exhibition, as the Salvator Mundi carved by Gian Lorenzo Bernini in 1679. The identification was argued by Francesco Petrucci in the Bollettino d'Arte and rests on the scale and on the Sicilian jasper of the pedestal; versions at the Chrysler Museum in Norfolk and at Sees cathedral have also been proposed for the same work.

places.name: Museo dei Sarcofagi
places.summary: A collection of local sarcophagi held in the room on the right of the modern church of San Sebastiano fuori le mura, the same room that gives access to the catacomb below. The operator states that the room on the left, which holds the Cappella del Crocifisso and the epigraphic museum, is under restoration and closed to the public.
places.history: No source states a separate institutional history of the collection.

places.name: Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine
places.summary: The pozzolana quarries on via Ardeatina where German occupation forces shot 335 people on 24 March 1944, in reprisal for the partisan attack in via Rasella, and the memorial built over them. Entry from via Ardeatina is through a bronze gate about six metres long by Mirko Basaldella, finished in 1951, with two smaller versions inside. Just within stands Francesco Coccia's travertine group Le tre eta, a young man, an adult and an old man, on a base of stone tuff from Monte Compatri. The forecourt is dedicated to the dead of the Marzabotto massacre and carries a Christian cross and a Star of David. Inside the galleries are two chasms opened by the explosives the SS set to hide the bodies. The sacrario is a hollow reinforced-concrete monolith on a rectangular plan, 26.65 by 48.5 by 3.55 metres, sunk two metres into the ground so that a thin slit of light runs between base and cover, about 1,300 square metres carried on six supports along the long edges. It holds 335 granite sacelli, in seven double rows in the order the bodies were exhumed, plus one dedicated to the Martiri d'Italia; 328 of the dead are identified and seven are unknown, and 70 of the 335 were Jews. A votive lamp given by Paul VI stands at the end of the gallery. Open Monday to Friday 08:15 to 15:15 and Saturday and Sunday 08:15 to 16:45.
places.history: The Commissione per le Cave Ardeatine was set up on 10 June 1944 under the American colonel Charles Poletti; the city council approved the competition notice on 15 January 1945 with a fifty-day deadline; eleven projects, anonymous and identified by motto, were submitted by 10 April 1945 and shown at the Casa dei Cavalieri di Rodi. On 2 September 1946 the second stage ended with two winners ex aequo: Risorgere, by Nello Aprile, Cino Calcaprina, Aldo Cardelli and Mario Fiorentino with the sculptor Francesco Coccia, and U.G.A., by Giuseppe Perugini with Uga de Plaisant, the two teams later joined by the sculptor Mirko Basaldella. The Ministry of Public Works allocated 70 million lire and then a further 130 million. Building began on 22 November 1947 and the complex was inaugurated on 24 March 1949, the fifth anniversary. The site is run by the Ufficio per la tutela della cultura e della memoria della difesa of the Ministry of Defence with ANFIM, the Associazione nazionale tra le famiglie italiane dei martiri caduti per la liberta della Patria, which also runs the guided visits: info@anfim.org, +39 06 6795629.

places.name: Museo dei cimeli
places.summary: A museum inside the Fosse Ardeatine complex, behind the monumental slab, holding documents, relics and photographs that reconstruct the historical context of the massacre of 24 March 1944. It keeps the hours of the mausoleum: Monday to Friday 08:15 to 15:15, Saturday and Sunday 08:15 to 16:45.
places.history: The museum is run within the complex by the Ufficio per la tutela della cultura e della memoria della difesa of the Ministry of Defence, working with ANFIM.

places.name: Monumento ai caduti della Montagnola
places.address: Piazzale dei Caduti della Montagnola, Roma RM
places.summary: A war memorial standing in the square of the Montagnola, surrounded by a public park, on the same piazzale as the church of Gesu Buon Pastore.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that the monument was raised after the war for the dead of 10 September 1943, when this quartiere, like other areas south of the city, saw fighting between the resisting population and the nazifascists in the days after the armistice.

places.name: Abbazia delle Tre Fontane
places.address: Via di Acque Salvie 1, Roma RM
places.summary: A walled monastic complex of three churches off via Laurentina, with the character of a fortified monastery and an entrance arch known as the Arco di Carlo Magno. The abbey is Trappist — Cistercians of the Strict Observance. The name comes from the tradition that St Paul was beheaded here and that his head bounced three times, striking a spring from the ground at each bounce; the valley, crossed by the ancient via Laurentina, has been called Aquae Salviae since at least the sixth century. The community also keeps an olive grove, an oil mill, an apiary and a farm, and brews beer sold through the monastic shop. The complex is open every day 06:30 to 20:45. The porter's lodge opens Monday to Saturday 08:30 to 12:30 and 15:00 to 18:00, and Sunday 08:30 to 09:30, 11:00 to 12:30 and 15:30 to 18:00; telephone +39 06 5401655.
places.history: A Greek-Armenian monastery here is attested at the synod of Martin I in 649, and the emperor Heraclius sent it the head of the Persian martyr Anastasius. Monastery and church burned at the end of the eighth century and were restored. Gregory VII gave the house to the Cluniacs around 1080; Innocent II took it from them in 1140 and gave it to the Cistercians, and the abbey church and monastery as they now stand date from that period. A document of 1161 names all three churches together. A Cistercian abbot of the house became Pope Eugene III. The monastery was completed in 1306 and acquired the relics of Vincent of Saragossa, who became co-titular, in 1370. Martin V turned it into a commenda in 1408. The French suppressed it in 1808 and sacked it, its books and archives going to the Vatican and Casanatense libraries and the site left malarial and ruined. Pius IX found funds for its restoration for the jubilee of 1867, and a bull of 1868 re-established a resident community of at least fourteen and handed the abbey to Trappist monks, who took 450 hectares of the Acque Salvie in perpetual emphyteusis on condition of planting 125,000 eucalypts to drain the ground. On 25 March 1981, by the bull Abbatia SS. Vincentii et Anastasii, John Paul II suppressed the territorial abbacy and the abbey passed to the diocese of Rome.

places.name: Chiesa dei Santi Vincenzo e Anastasio alle Tre Fontane
places.address: Via di Acque Salvie 1, Roma RM
places.summary: The conventual church of the Tre Fontane, where the community keeps its offices. Its foundation goes back to the seventh century in origin, while the fabric belongs to the Cistercian rebuilding after 1140. It keeps a medieval fresco cycle. Open every day 06:30 to 20:45.
places.history: The church takes its double dedication from Vincent of Saragossa, whose relics reached the abbey in 1370, and from the Persian martyr Anastasius, whose head was sent to the Greek-Armenian monastery here by the emperor Heraclius. The bull of 25 March 1981 that suppressed the territorial abbacy was named for the two saints.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria Scala Coeli
places.address: Via di Acque Salvie 1, Roma RM
places.summary: The second of the three churches in the Tre Fontane complex, on an octagonal plan. Open every day 09:00 to 12:00 and 15:00 to 17:30.
places.history: Its foundation goes back to the Greek-Armenian monastery attested here in the seventh century, dedicated to the Virgin; the present building is of the sixteenth century.

places.name: Chiesa di San Paolo alle Tre Fontane
places.address: Via di Acque Salvie 1, Roma RM
places.summary: The third church of the Tre Fontane complex, which the abbey's own site calls San Paolo al Martirio, the church of the martyrdom of St Paul. It stands over the springs of the beheading tradition. The abbey announces that the church is open again, every day 07:30 to 20:00.
places.history: The present building is of the sixteenth century. Filippo Neri briefly added it, with the Chiesa dell'Annunziatella, to the itinerary of the Seven Churches, which thereby became nine.

places.name: Negozio monastico dell'Abbazia delle Tre Fontane
places.address: Via di Acque Salvie 1, Roma RM
places.summary: The abbey's shop, inside the monastic complex, selling the community's own produce, including the beer it brews. Open Monday to Saturday 08:30 to 19:30 without a midday break, and Sunday 09:00 to 13:30.
places.history: The beer carries the International Trappist Association's certification mark Authentic Trappist Product, which is the mark of a private trade body. The abbey's site records the renewal of that certification. No source states any brewery visit, taproom or public access to the brewhouse, so none is described here: the beer reaches visitors through this shop.

places.name: Caffe Tre Fontane
places.address: Via di Acque Salvie 1, Roma RM
places.summary: A cafe inside the grounds of the Abbazia delle Tre Fontane, carried on the abbey's own menu of what stands in the complex. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: No source states a history of the cafe.

places.name: Ente Regionale Parco dell'Appia Antica
places.summary: The regional park authority, with its headquarters and visitor centre in the buildings of the former Cartiera Latina paper mill on via Appia Antica. The park it administers extends well beyond this quartiere. The authority runs bicycle hire on the Appia; no address is stated for it, so none is given here. The green area and car park at the headquarters open every day 08:30 to 17:00 in winter and 08:30 to 19:00 in summer, with tables and benches free to use, no reserving them and no events without authorisation. Telephone +39 06 512 6314.
places.history: The site of the Cartiera Latina was granted to the regional park in 1998 as its headquarters and a multi-purpose visitor centre. The Via Appia was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2024 as Via Appia. Regina Viarum, a serial property of nineteen component parts inscribed under criteria (iii), (iv) and (vi). The road was constructed and developed from 312 BCE to the 4th century CE and runs more than 800 kilometres. A separate state body, the Parco archeologico dell'Appia antica of the Ministero della cultura, also operates in the quartiere and is not the same institution.

places.name: Ex Cartiera Latina
places.summary: A paper mill turned into the regional park's headquarters, with a multimedia museum in the halls that still hold the original machinery: the Sala macchine, the Sala della macchina continua, the Sala Nagasawa and the Sala Appia. An audio guide and a QR-code route funded by Regione Lazio run through them, and paper-making workshops are run by booking. The other pavilions hold the park authority's offices, the Biblioteca della Cartiera Latina 'Fabrizio Giucca', the sala conferenze 'Antonio Cederna', a meeting room and teaching laboratories. Outdoors there are two exhibition rooms for hire, a park information point with a bookshop run by Di Natura, and the Hortus Urbis teaching garden. The river Almone runs the length of the site. Green area and car park open every day 08:30 to 17:00 in winter and 08:30 to 19:00 in summer.
places.history: Production on this spot goes back to 1081, to a fulling mill for wool cloth called the valca; the Capuchins used the site from the 1600s. In December 1804 it ground vallonea for tanning, in 1823 myrtle for medicines, and in 1875 pigments for ceramics. In 1919 the mill became an industrial paper works with a steam boiler and three electric motors totalling 67 amperes. The Societa anonima per azioni Cartiera Appia was formed in September 1923 and became the Societa Anonima Cartiera Latina in January 1931. In the 1930s it made quality paper for publishing from cotton rags, and from the late 1940s, the Almone having become polluted, it switched to recycled stock. The factory closed in 1986. In 1998 the site was granted in concession to the regional park.

places.name: Hortus Urbis
places.summary: Hortus Urbis is a teaching garden at the Cartiera Latina, described by the park authority as an educational area, also for schools, dedicated to the traditions of the Campagna Romana. It lies inside the green area of the park headquarters, which opens every day 08:30 to 17:00 in winter and 08:30 to 19:00 in summer.
places.history: No source states a separate history of the garden.

places.name: Complesso di Capo di Bove
places.summary: A green plot of about 8,600 square metres at the IV mile of the via Appia Antica, about 500 metres from the Mausoleo di Cecilia Metella, with a three-storey main building and a smaller one. Excavation of the garden uncovered a bath complex of the middle of the second century AD, with building phases running to the fourth and traces of late-antique agricultural use, when the area formed part of the Patrimonium Appiae: dozens of rooms, mosaic and coloured-marble floors, water tanks, terracotta tubuli, the drainage system, and stretches of marble revetment and painted plaster. The main building stands on the Roman cistern that fed the baths, with a curtain wall of reused ancient material built in the 1950s. Since 22 June 2026 the complex has been temporarily closed to the public to allow restoration works on the reception building, the gardens and the baths area to begin, and no reopening date has been announced.
places.history: The property came up for sale in 2002 and the Soprintendenza and the ministry bought it by exercising the right of pre-emption. When it is open, the Parco archeologico dell'Appia antica sells a combined ticket with the Mausoleo di Cecilia Metella at 8 euro full, 2 euro reduced and 4 euro with the Roma Pass, valid the same day; the mausoleum itself is not in this quartiere. A park ticket at 12 euro full and 2 euro reduced is valid seven days across the Antiquarium di Lucrezia Romana, the Mausoleo di Cecilia Metella, Capo di Bove, Villa dei Quintili with Santa Maria Nova, the Tombe della via Latina and the Villa di Sette Bassi, by booking; La Mia Appia Card costs 25 euro for a calendar year.

places.name: Archivio e Biblioteca di Antonio Cederna
places.summary: The archive and library of Antonio Cederna, a campaigner for the protection of the Via Appia Antica, are housed in the main building at Capo di Bove. The complex has been closed to the public since 22 June 2026.
places.history: The Parco archeologico dell'Appia antica gives the archive its own page among the places it administers.

places.name: Sepolcro di Priscilla
places.summary: A tomb of the first century at the II mile of the via Appia Antica, standing opposite the church of the Domine quo vadis on the far side of the road. Over a quadrangular travertine-faced base rose two superimposed cylindrical drums in opus reticulatum, the upper one carrying 13 niches for statues of the deified dead woman. The barrel-vaulted burial chamber is reached by a corridor now entered from the cellars of one of the farmhouses built against the monument. It can be visited on particular occasions.
places.history: Priscilla was the wife of Titus Flavius Abascantus, a freedman of Domitian and his secretary ab epistulis, and the tomb is identified from Statius, Silvae V, the Epicedion in Priscillam Abascanti Uxorem, which records that she was embalmed rather than cremated. In 1773 a marble slab was found beside the mausoleum, set up for the young slave Aphrodisius by T. Flavius Epaphroditus, custodian of the tomb for Abascantus and Priscilla; it reached the civic lapidary collection of Ferrara in 1779, by gift of Cardinal Gian Maria Riminaldi. From the eleventh century the monument was reused as a fortification, a cylindrical tower called the torre Petro being built on the upper drum; it was held by the counts of Tusculum and then by the Caetani. In the eighteenth century it was wrongly believed to be the tomb of the Scipios, and Piranesi drew it. Two farmhouses were later built against it, one of them the osteria dell'Acquataccio, and the burial chamber was used to age cheese.

places.name: Le tombe del IV miglio della via Appia Antica
places.summary: A sequence of roadside tombs standing within about 400 metres of one another at the IV mile of the via Appia Antica, where the boundary leaves the road and both sides fall in this quartiere. The individually identifiable ones are the Mausoleo di Sant'Urbano martire, of the second century; the Tomba dei Licini; the Tomba del fregio dorico, an altar-tomb of the Sullan period; the Sepolcro di Hilarus Fuscus; the Tomba di Tiberio Claudio Secondino; a colombario; the Tomba di Quinto Apuleio; a rectangular tomb in the form of a small temple; the Tomba dei Rabiri, of the first century; a tower tomb with an arched doorway; the Tomba dei Festoni; and the Tomba del frontespizio.
places.history: The tombs stand on the open stretch of the road beyond via Cecilia Metella, in the part of the Appia that this quartiere holds on both sides. At the III mile, on the same road, is a marble high relief carrying a figure in heroic nudity.

places.name: Villa di Tor Carbone
places.summary: The remains of a Roman villa of the first century at the IV mile of the via Appia Antica, also known as the Domus marmeniae. No visiting arrangements are stated for it, so none are given here.
places.history: The site is catalogued by Marina De Franceschini in Ville dell'Agro romano, L'Erma di Bretschneider, 2005, chapter 78, pages 217 to 219.

places.name: Tenuta di Tor Marancia
places.summary: Two hundred hectares of Roman countryside inside the city, bounded on the west by the natural edge of the Marrana dell'Annunziatella and on the north and east by Via delle Sette Chiese, Via Ardeatina and Vicolo dell'Annunziatella. There are three entrances: two off Via Giulio Aristide Sartorio, at Piazza Lante and at nearby Via Francesco Belloni, and a third from Viale Londra on the Grotta Perfetta side. The Parco archeologico dell'Appia antica states that the site is freely accessible.
places.history: Human traces here run back to the Middle Palaeolithic, from about 70,000 to 35,000 BC, and the land has been farmed from Roman times to the present. A Roman house of the middle of the second century stood on the estate, the Villa dei Numisii, which belonged to Numisia Procula, named on a stamped lead pipe found here; quarrying to the right of the via Ardeatina has since destroyed it. The name Tor Marancia probably comes from Amaranthus, the freedman who managed the Numisii villa. The Torre Marancia itself stood on via delle Sette Chiese near the Domitilla catacombs and had gone by the Catasto Alessandrino of 1660. Basolate roads, funerary monuments and necropoleis line the Ardeatina and the Laurentina, one of them along Via di Grotta Perfetta near the Chiesa dell'Annunziatella. Residential building inside the Grande Raccordo Anulare was planned from the 1990s and blocked after public campaigns, and in 2002 the city council and giunta resolved to create the Parco di Tor Marancia as part of the Appia Antica park.

places.name: Museo Condominiale di Tor Marancia
places.address: Viale di Tor Marancia 63, Roma RM
places.summary: Twenty-two monumental murals painted on eleven blocks of the ATER public-housing estate Lotto 1, and looked at from the street. Named works include Alberonero's A Carlo Alberto, 93 colori, acrylic, 10 by 14.5 metres; Caratoes's Welcome to Shangay, 5 by 5.3 metres; Mr Klevra's Nostra Signora di Shanghai; Diamond's Hic sunt adamantes; Gaia's Spettacolo, Rinnovamento, Maturita; Domenico Romeo's Alme sol invictus; Danilo Bucchi's Assolo; Best Ever's Piramide; and an untitled work by Clemens Behr.
places.history: The estate dates from 1947. The project was conceived in 2013 by Stefano Antonelli with Gianluca Marziani consulting, and carried out in 2014 and 2015 by the association 999Contemporary under the name Big City Life: 70 working days, 765 litres of paint and 974 spray cans. It was funded 55 per cent by 999Contemporary, 25 per cent by the Fondazione Roma and 20 per cent by Roma Capitale through the Roma Creativa public call, under a protocol with ATER and sponsored by Municipio Roma VIII, with ATAC, Sikkens and Pescerosso. It opened officially on 9 March 2015, and in 2016 represented Italy in the Italian Pavilion at the 15th Venice Architecture Biennale, Taking Care - Progettare per il bene comune. ICOM recognises it as museum institution no. M124582; it is run by the Museo Condominiale di Tor Marancia association, chaired by Antonelli and directed by Marziani.

places.name: Forte Ardeatino
places.address: Via di Grotta Perfetta, Roma RM
places.summary: One of the fifteen forts built round Rome between 1877 and 1891, of the Prussian type and part of the Campo trincerato di Roma. It was built between 1879 and 1882 over 11.2 hectares at the fourth kilometre of via Ardeatina, from which it takes its name. Its own article places it in the quartiere Q. XX Ardeatino, in the territory of Municipio Roma VIII. In May 2006, after restoration work, the park outside the fort was opened to the public; the interior of the fort is still not accessible.
places.history: From the 1920s the fort served as a military commissariat and a health-service store. It was decommissioned in 1961 and assigned in concession to the Ente Assistenza Cancerosi Poveri, a plan that came to nothing. It was handed to the Comune di Roma in 1982, with an expropriation never completed, and is now owned by Roma Capitale.

places.name: Forte Appia Antica
places.summary: One of the fifteen forts built round Rome between 1877 and 1891, standing at the fourth kilometre of via Appia Antica. Work began in 1877 and finished in 1880, over more than 16.5 hectares. Its own article places it in the quartiere Q. XX Ardeatino, in the territory of Municipio Roma VIII. No public access is stated, so none is described here.
places.history: Until the 1910s the fort housed the Artillery Directorate of the Corpo Aeronautico. Between the 1980s and the 1990s it was the data-processing centre of the Aeronautica Militare's Reparto Sistemi Informativi Automatizzati, which still uses part of it as a store.

places.name: I casali della campagna ardeatina
places.summary: Five farmhouses standing in the open country of the quartiere. They are the Casale de Merode, also called Casale di Tor Marancia, on via delle Sette Chiese; the Casale della Vignacce of the seventeenth century, on vicolo di Tor Carbone in the tenuta Muracci dell'Ospedaletto; the Casale di Vigna Viola of the eighteenth century, on via Ardeatina in the tenuta Zampa di Bove; the Casale Torlonia of the seventeenth century, at the III mile of via Appia Antica; and the Casale Caribelli of the eighteenth century, on viale Pico della Mirandola. No visiting arrangements are stated for any of them, so none are given here.
places.history: The sources give a century for four of the five. For the Casale de Merode the source reading is internally doubtful, so no century is given.

places.name: Chiesa dell'Annunziatella
places.summary: A small church on the vicolo that carries its name, between via Ardeatina and via di Grotta Perfetta. It has a single nave, a nineteenth-century wooden Crucifix, and a tripartite fresco in the apse conch with an Annunciation at the centre and a Madonna among the souls in purgatory and a Nativity at the sides.
places.history: An inscription inside the church, dated 12 August 1220 and issued by Honorius III, lists it among the Roman churches named for Maria Annunziata, which is where the popular diminutive comes from. For a short period Filippo Neri added it, together with San Paolo alle Tre Fontane, to the itinerary of the Seven Churches, which thereby became nine, and a hospice served the pilgrims who came. In 1640 Cardinal Francesco Barberini, protector of the Confraternita del Gonfalone to which the church was entrusted, reduced it to its present form, and the tradition of distributing food to the poor on 25 March began.

places.name: Chiesa della Santissima Annunziata a Via Ardeatina
places.address: Via di Grotta Perfetta, Roma RM
places.summary: A parish church of 1987 on via di Grotta Perfetta, by the engineer Ignazio Breccia Fratadocchi.
places.history: Ancient artefacts came to light during the excavation for the building.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Francesca Romana (Ardeatino)
places.summary: A rationalist church of 1936 on via Augusto Franzoi, by the architect Giuseppe Zander. It shares its dedication with a basilica in the rione Campitelli and is a different building.
places.history: The parish was erected on 23 May 1959 by the decree Supremam in Ecclesia of Cardinal Vicar Clemente Micara.

places.name: Chiesa di San Vigilio
places.address: Via Paolo di Dono, Roma RM
places.summary: A modernist parish church of 1990 on via Paolo di Dono, by the architect Lucio Passarelli.
places.history: The parish was erected on 22 May 1968 by the decree Quotidianis curis of Cardinal Vicar Angelo Dell'Acqua.

places.name: Chiesa dei Santi Martiri dell'Uganda
places.address: Largo Santi Martiri dell'Uganda, Roma RM
places.summary: A parish church of 1971 on the largo that carries its name.
places.history: The parish was erected on 4 September 1970 by the decree Pervigili cura of Cardinal Vicar Angelo Dell'Acqua.

places.name: Chiesa di Gesu Buon Pastore
places.address: Piazzale dei Caduti della Montagnola, Roma RM
places.summary: A church built between 1950 and 1957 on the piazzale dei Caduti della Montagnola, on the same square as the war memorial of the Montagnola.
places.history: No source states a further institutional history of the church.

places.name: Chiesa di Nostra Signora di Lourdes a Tor Marancia
places.summary: A parish church of 1957 on via Andrea Mantegna, in the Tor Marancia housing quarter.
places.history: No source states a further institutional history of the church.

places.name: Chiesa di San Josemaria Escriva
places.address: Largo Josemaria Escriva de Balaguer, Roma RM
places.summary: A church of 1996 on the largo that carries the same name.
places.history: No source states a further institutional history of the church.

places.name: Baby Luna Park
places.address: Via di Grotta Perfetta 555, 00142 Roma RM
places.summary: Baby Luna Park is a covered amusement park and playground at Via di Grotta Perfetta 555, 00142 Roma. It is open on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays, 10:00 to 20:00.
places.history: No source states a history of the park that publishes here.

entries.name: Catacombe di San Callisto
entries.note: Sixteen popes and more than fifty martyrs, the Cripta dei Papi with its original Greek inscriptions, and the crypt of St Cecilia; tours every 30 minutes, closed Wednesdays.

entries.name: Catacombe di San Sebastiano
entries.note: Three levels of galleries, three mausolea in the old quarry piazzola, and the triclia whose walls carry more than 600 graffiti invoking Peter and Paul.

entries.name: Basilica di San Sebastiano fuori le mura
entries.note: The Cappella delle Reliquie of 1625 holds the stone of the 'Quo Vadis?' episode with the footprints impressed in it, along with an arrow of the martyrdom.

entries.name: Catacombe di Domitilla
entries.note: Dug in the estate of Flavia Domitilla, with a Siricius-era basilica over the tombs of Nereus and Achilleus, and Christian and pagan burials side by side.

entries.name: Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine
entries.note: The quarries where 335 people were shot on 24 March 1944, under a concrete sacrario holding 335 granite sacelli; inaugurated on the fifth anniversary in 1949.

entries.name: Museo dei cimeli
entries.note: Documents, relics and photographs reconstructing the context of the massacre, inside the mausoleum complex behind the monumental slab.

entries.name: Abbazia delle Tre Fontane
entries.note: A Trappist house of Cistercians of the Strict Observance with three churches, on the valley the sources have called Aquae Salviae since the sixth century; open daily 06:30 to 20:45.

entries.name: Negozio monastico dell'Abbazia delle Tre Fontane
entries.note: The abbey's own produce, including the beer it brews, sold Monday to Saturday 08:30 to 19:30 and Sunday morning; no brewery visit is stated anywhere.

entries.name: Caffe Tre Fontane
entries.note: A cafe inside the abbey grounds, carried on the abbey's own menu of the complex; no source states its opening hours.

entries.name: Ex Cartiera Latina
entries.note: A paper mill with a documented chain of use back to a fulling mill of 1081, now the regional park's headquarters with a museum in the old machine halls.

entries.name: Tenuta di Tor Marancia
entries.note: Two hundred hectares of Roman countryside with three entrances, farmed since Roman times and freely accessible according to the state park.

entries.name: Museo Condominiale di Tor Marancia
entries.note: Twenty-two murals painted on eleven housing blocks in 2014 and 2015, opened on 9 March 2015 and registered by ICOM as museum institution no. M124582.

entries.name: Le tombe del IV miglio della via Appia Antica
entries.note: A sequence of roadside tombs within about 400 metres of one another, among them the Tomba dei Rabiri, the Tomba del fregio dorico and the Tomba dei Festoni.

entries.name: Complesso di Capo di Bove
entries.note: Roman baths of the mid-second century in an 8,600 square metre garden, closed to the public since 22 June 2026 for restoration, with no reopening date announced.

links.note: The neighbouring quartiere west across via Cristoforo Colombo, holding San Paolo fuori le Mura and the Centrale Montemartini.
The neighbour across via Laurentina, the declared line between the two quartieri; the Tre Fontane abbey stands on this side of it.
The rione immediately north, inside the Aurelian Walls, which holds Porta San Paolo and the Museo della Via Ostiense.
The other rione on the northern boundary, inside the walls between Porta San Sebastiano and the Colosseum.
The three-day Rome itinerary in this series, for fitting a morning on the Appia around the centre.
